KIDS GAMES LESSON · KIDS GAMES · AGES 3–5 YEARS

Fishing — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches the fishing game — a paper pond, a magnet rod, and the steadiest hands in the house.

What is this?

The fishing game is a catching game: paper fish with paper-clip mouths swim on the floor, and a magnet-on-a-string rod lifts them out.

What does it mean?

The magnet does not hurry, so neither can the fisher — steady hands and patience are the whole catch.

What does the child need to know?

You need paper fish (cut simple fish shapes), one paper clip per fish, a stick, string and a small magnet. The floor is the pond.

Why this matters

Waiting for the clip to meet the magnet is a patience practice that ends in a genuine, satisfying CLICK — the best small win in quiet games.

What it teaches

Steady-hand control, patience and waiting, hand-eye targeting at a distance, and counting the catch.

Words to learn

fishrodlinehookcatchpondcount

Say this to your child

“"Hold the rod steady... let the line dangle... wait for it... wait for it... GOT ONE! You caught the pink fish! Into the bucket — now pass the rod on."”

Step by step

  1. Make the pond: scatter the paper fish on the floor, clips facing up.
  2. Make the rod: tie the string to the stick, tie the magnet to the string.
  3. Hold the rod with two hands and dangle the magnet over a fish.
  4. Hold VERY still — wait for the magnet and clip to find each other. CLICK!
  5. Lift the fish out and into your bucket, then pass the rod to the next fisher. Count the catch at the end.

Look closer at the picture

On the card, the rod hooks one leaping fish while more fish swim in the little pond — the leaping one is the moment the clip meets the magnet.

Ask your child

"Why must we hold still?" (so the magnet can catch the clip) "How many fish did you catch?" "Which fish is the biggest?"

What your child can say or do

Your child might narrate every catch like a deep-sea captain, name all the fish, or hold the rod with tongue-out concentration that makes the waiting worth watching.

Out in the real world

Magnetic fishing rods come with every fishing-game set at every toy shop — and now your child can build the pond version from paper whenever the real one is out of reach.

Try it together

Two-rod round if waiting gets wobbly — one rod each, divided pond. Colors round: "catch only the pink fish!" Counting round: land exactly three fish, no more.

Understanding check

Ask: "What makes the fish stick to the line?" (the magnet and the paper clip) "What do we do after our catch?" (lift it out, bucket it, pass the rod)

This lesson pairs with the Fishing flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Kids Games.
